name: Aztreonam
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Aztreonam is excreted in urine by both filtration and tubular secretion, and its half-life is prolonged in kidney impairment. The US label gives a usual 1 or 2 g loading dose, then half the usual dose at creatinine clearance (CrCl) 10–30 mL/min/1.73 m2 and one-quarter below 10, with an extra one-eighth of the initial dose after each hemodialysis in serious infections.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses CrCl in mL/min/1.73 m2 (formula quoted); bands at 30 and 10. The mL/min/1.73 m2 unit is the label's own convention and is kept verbatim.

bands.recommendation: No dose change above CrCl 30. At CrCl 30: as the 10–30 row (initial 1 or 2 g, then half the usual dose) (label).
CrCl 10–30: initial 1 or 2 g, then half the usual dose at the usual interval (label).
CrCl 10–14: initial 1 or 2 g, then half the usual dose. Below 10: usual initial dose (500 mg, 1 g or 2 g), then one-fourth of the initial dose at the usual 6-, 8- or 12-hour interval (label).

hd.text: Usual initial dose (500 mg, 1 g or 2 g), then one-fourth of the initial dose at the usual 6-, 8- or 12-hour interval; for serious or life-threatening infections, also give one-eighth of the initial dose after each hemodialysis (label).

pd.text: No peritoneal dialysis dosing in label (aztreonam can be cleared by peritoneal dialysis, overdose section). IV aztreonam rapidly reaches therapeutic levels in peritoneal dialysis fluid, and intraperitoneal aztreonam rapidly produces therapeutic serum levels (label PK); the label gives no dose. For PD-associated peritonitis (ISPD 2022): intraperitoneal intermittent 2 g daily; continuous loading dose 500 mg/L, then 250 mg/L in each exchange. Specialist input.

crrt.text: Not in label; the cited CRRT review (Li 2020) gives no regimen for this drug. Specialist input.
crrt.short: No CRRT data in cited sources

dialyzable: Yes: may be cleared by hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis (label). Protein binding about 56%.
monitoring: CrCl for dose (serum creatinine may overestimate kidney function in older adults; label); diarrhea (CDAD).

pediatric.usual_dose: Mild to moderate infections: 30 mg/kg every 8 hours; moderate to severe: 30 mg/kg every 6 or 8 hours (label).

renal.recommendation: Insufficient data on dosing in children with kidney impairment (label). Specialist input.
